mainTopic: Whether a נזיר who vowed in a cemetery shaves and brings birds, and the מחלוקת of רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה over when pure נזירות restarts (the seventh or the eighth day).
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב אשי's question: if someone becomes a נזיר while already in a cemetery, does he shave and bring birds when he becomes pure? An earlier proof from a ברייתא about a מצורע is pushed away. A new ברייתא then reads "וטמא ראש נזרו" as speaking only about a נזיר who was pure and became impure. It even sets aside a קל וחומר that pointed the other way, so the נזיר in a grave is exempt, and the גמרא says שמע מינה. Next, רב חסדא identifies the authors of two sources. One is a ברייתא saying that the seventh day counts for a טמא שנזר but not for a נזיר טהור שנטמא, and רב חסדא says it follows רבי, who holds that pure נזירות restarts only on the eighth day. The other is a משנה saying that many impurities need only one קרבן, and he says it follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who restarts pure נזירות on the seventh day. The source for their מחלוקת is a ברייתא on "וקדש את ראשו ביום ההוא". Finally, the גמרא shows that רבי learns from the order of the פסוק, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה pushes back on that reading.

steps.title: Why the earlier ברייתא must mean the shaving of purity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier proof. The ברייתא calls a מצורע unfit for shaving, so it cannot mean shaving of טומאה, because a confirmed מצורע does shave.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you thought the ברייתא was talking about the shaving done because of impurity, then there is a problem: doesn't a confirmed מצורע also need to shave?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier attempt to answer רב אשי's question. It explains why an earlier ברייתא must be talking about the shaving done at the end of a pure נזירות, and not about shaving because of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא described a מצורע as unfit for shaving. A confirmed מצורע does shave when his leprosy ends, so the ברייתא cannot mean that kind of shaving. So the argument says it must mean the shaving of purity, and that would help settle the question about the נזיר in a cemetery.

keyTerms.meaning: For if it would enter your mind: an opening that shows why another reading cannot work
The shaving a נזיר does because he became impure
The days of his confirmed leprosy (a מצורע מוחלט)
Shaving, a ritual shaving of the hair

phrases.english: For if it would enter your mind
that it means the shaving of impurity,

phrases.aramaic: יְמֵי חִלּוּטוֹ מִי לָא בָּעֵי תִּגְלַחַת?
phrases.english: do the days of his confirmed leprosy not require shaving?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof attempt begun just before this section (on 17b).
steps.raayaObject: That the earlier ברייתא speaks about the shaving of purity, which would help answer רב אשי's question.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A confirmed מצורע does shave, so "unfit for shaving" cannot mean shaving of טומאה.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא means a נזיר's shaving
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. The ברייתא could mean that a מצורע is unfit for any shaving of נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The ברייתא is teaching about the shaving of נזירות, and that is what the מצורע is unfit for.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 1. The ברייתא can be read differently, so it proves nothing about our question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Unfit for shaving" does not have to mean "never shaves at all." It can mean the מצורע cannot do a נזיר's shaving, because his own leprosy shaving comes first. Once that reading is possible, the ברייתא no longer shows which kind of shaving it is talking about, so the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: No: the proof is rejected
The shaving that belongs to נזירות
It is teaching: the ברייתא is speaking about

phrases.english: No, it is teaching about the shaving of nezirus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the מצורע ברייתא. רב אשי's question is not settled by this ברייתא; a new proof follows in step 3 and is accepted in step 6.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as talking about a נזיר's shaving in general, so it does not decide between shaving of טומאה and shaving of purity.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: the פסוק speaks only about a pure נזיר who became impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads "וטמא ראש נזרו" as speaking only about a נזיר who was pure and then became impure. That reading exempts a נזיר who was in a grave from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "And he defiles his consecrated head." The פסוק speaks about a pure person who became impure. He must remove his hair and bring birds. This comes to exempt the נזיר who was in a grave: he does not need to remove his hair or bring birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof for רב אשי's question by quoting a ברייתא that directly talks about a נזיר in a grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "וטמא" ("and he defiles") suggests that he was pure first and then became impure. So the ברייתא says only that kind of נזיר shaves and brings birds. A נזיר who was already impure when he made his vow is left out. That is exactly רב אשי's case.

keyTerms.meaning: A pure person who became impure
Removal of hair (the shaving)
Bringing of birds as offerings
A נזיר who took his vow while in a grave or cemetery

phrases.english: Come and hear:

the verse is speaking about a pure person who became impure,
who requires removal of hair
and bringing of birds.
And this comes to exempt the nazir in a grave
phrases.notes: He means someone who became a נזיר while he was already in a cemetery, so he was impure from the very start.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין טָעוּן הַעֲבָרַת שֵׂעָר וַהֲבָאַת צִיפֳּרִין.
phrases.english: that he does not require removal of hair and bringing of birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new proof is brought.
steps.raayaObject: That a נזיר who vowed in a cemetery does not shave or bring birds.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading of "וטמא ראש נזרו" (במדבר 6:9).

steps.title: A קל וחומר that seems to require him to shave
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, a challenge is raised. If a pure person who became impure must shave and bring birds, then someone impure from the start should need it even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't this a קל וחומר? If a pure person who became impure needs to remove his hair and bring birds, then someone who was impure from the start should surely need to remove his hair and bring birds too!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a logical argument against its own reading. A קל וחומר seems to show the opposite: the נזיר in a grave should need to shave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic says that someone who was "more impure", impure from the very beginning, should not get an easier rule than someone who only became impure later. If this argument stood, the exemption from step 3 would fall. The ברייתא now needs to show why the פסוק overrides this logic.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a heavier case: if the rule applies there, it surely applies here
But are these matters not...: the opening of a logical challenge
Impure from the start
Is it not logical?

steps.confusionAlert: This קל וחומר is NOT the final הלכה. The ברייתא raises it only to show that the פסוק overrides it.

phrases.english: But are these matters not an a fortiori argument?
If a pure person who became impure
requires removal of hair and bringing of birds,
then one who was impure from the start,
is it not logical

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהֵא טָעוּן הַעֲבָרַת שֵׂעָר וַהֲבָאַת צִיפֳּרִין?
phrases.english: that he should require removal of hair and bringing of birds?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the exemption that the ברייתא just stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: The exemption of the נזיר in a grave (step 3).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a lesser impurity (pure, then impure) requires shaving and birds, then a greater one (impure from the start) should require them even more.

steps.title: The פסוק overrides the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the פסוק "וטמא ראש נזרו" deliberately limits shaving and birds to one who was pure and became impure. That exempts the נזיר in a grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says "And he defiles his consecrated head." It speaks about one who was pure and became impure, and he is the one who needs to remove his hair and bring birds. It comes to exempt the נזיר in a grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the קל וחומר by pointing back to the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic cannot override what the פסוק clearly teaches. "וטמא" describes a change from pure to impure. So the תורה itself limits the obligation to that case, even though the קל וחומר seemed to point the other way.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches: the answer comes from the wording of the פסוק
The verse is speaking about

steps.whatToRemember: A פסוק's precise wording ("וטמא", became impure) beats a קל וחומר. Only a נזיר who was pure and then became impure shaves and brings birds.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "And he defiles his consecrated head,"
about one who was pure and became impure
the verse is speaking,
that he should require removal of hair
and bringing of birds,
and to exempt the nazir in a grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר from step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By קל וחומר, one who was impure from the start should need shaving and birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק limits the obligation to one who was pure and became impure, so the נזיר in a grave is exempt.

steps.title: Learn from it: the question is answered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא proves a נזיר who vowed in a cemetery does not shave or bring birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof from the ברייתא and closes רב אשי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time no one pushes the proof away. The ברייתא directly says the נזיר in a grave is exempt, so the question is settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: A נזיר who took his vow while in a cemetery does not do the טומאה shaving or bring birds.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers רב אשי's question. The obligations of a טמא נזיר depend on going from טהרה to טומאה, and not just on being impure.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the ברייתא from steps 3 to 5 as a proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A נזיר who vowed while in a cemetery does not need hair removal or the bird offerings.

steps.title: Who wrote the ברייתא about the seventh day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא taught the ברייתא that the seventh day counts for a טמא שנזר but not for a נזיר טהור שנטמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught this ברייתא? The only difference between someone who was impure when he took a vow of נזירות and a pure נזיר who became impure is this: for the first, his seventh day counts toward his days of נזירות; for the second, his seventh day does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא and asks which תנא it follows. This sets up רב חסדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both people go through a seven-day purification. The ברייתא says the seventh day counts as a day of נזירות for one of them but not for the other. The גמרא wants to know whose opinion makes that difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Who taught this? (asking which תנא is the author)
Someone who was already impure when he took a vow of נזירות
A נזיר who was pure and then became impure
Counts for him toward the number of נזירות days

steps.confusionAlert: Both people are purifying for seven days. The question is only whether the seventh day itself also counts as a day of נזירות.

phrases.english: Who taught this that the Rabbis taught:
There is no difference between an impure person who vowed נזירות
and a pure נזיר who became impure,
except that an impure person who vowed —

phrases.english: his seventh day counts for him toward the tally,
but a pure נזיר who became impure —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שְׁבִיעִי שֶׁלּוֹ עוֹלֶה לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן?
phrases.english: his seventh day does not count for him toward the tally?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After concluding that a נזיר who vowed in a cemetery does not shave or bring birds, the גמרא moves to another difference between him and a pure נזיר who became impure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the seventh day counts for a טמא שנזר but not for a נזיר טהור שנטמא?

steps.title: רב חסדא: the ברייתא follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the ברייתא is רבי, who holds that pure נזירות starts only on the eighth day. It cannot be רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who starts it on the seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי, because רבי said that pure נזירות takes effect only from the eighth day. If you say it is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, he says pure נזירות already takes effect from the seventh day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא names the author of the ברייתא as רבי. He explains why it cannot be רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, a נזיר who became impure restarts his pure counting only on the eighth day, so his seventh day does not count. The טמא שנזר brings no birds and no eighth-day קרבנות, so his seventh day does count. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה starts the pure counting on the seventh day for both, so for him the ברייתא's difference would not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: נזירות kept in purity (the real counting of the נזירות days)
Takes effect, begins to apply
For if you would say

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the ברייתא's rule to one side of a real מחלוקת about when pure נזירות starts again.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said: It is רבי,
for רבי said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נְזִירוּת טׇהֳרָה חָלָה אֶלָּא עַד שְׁמִינִי.
phrases.english: Pure נזירות takes effect only from the eighth day.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: For if you say it is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה,
doesn't he say that pure נזירות
takes effect from the seventh day?
phrases.notes: So for him the seventh day would count for both people, and the ברייתא's difference would fall away.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is רבי, who holds that pure נזירות starts only on the eighth day. It is not רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who starts it on the seventh.

steps.title: Where do these two opinions come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the opinions of רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה are recorded.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the statement of רבי, and what is the statement of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the two opinions רב חסדא just used. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא relied on a מחלוקת without quoting it. The גמרא now wants to see exactly where it appears.

keyTerms.meaning: What is

phrases.english: What is the statement of רבי,
and what is the statement of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רַבִּי וּמַאי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinions cited in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source text for the מחלוקת of רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה about when pure נזירות starts again.

steps.title: The ברייתא on 'he shall sanctify his head on that day'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the פסוק 'וקדש את ראשו ביום ההוא'. רבי reads it as the day of the קרבנות, the eighth day. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה reads it as the day of shaving, the seventh day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'And he shall sanctify his head on that day.' This means on the day he brings his קרבנות, according to רבי. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: on the day of his shaving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא where רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argue over what 'that day' means in the פסוק. This is the source of their two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Sanctify his head' means his נזירות in purity starts again. For רבי that happens on the day of the קרבנות, which is the eighth day. For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה it happens on the shaving day, which is the seventh.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall sanctify his head: his נזירות starts again
The bringing of his קרבנות (on the eighth day)
His shaving (on the seventh day)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: pure נזירות restarts on the eighth day (the קרבנות). רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: it restarts on the seventh day (the shaving).

phrases.english: As it is taught:
'And he shall sanctify his head on that day'
on the day he brings his offerings; these are the words of רבי.
רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says:
on the day of his shaving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by quoting the source ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא on במדבר 6:11: רבי says the day of the קרבנות, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the day of shaving.

steps.title: Who wrote the משנה about many impurities and one קרבן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא taught the משנה that a נזיר who became impure many times brings only one קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this that we learned in a משנה: a נזיר who became impure with many impurities brings only one קרבן. Who taught it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a משנה and asks whose opinion it follows. This sets up רב חסדא's second answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that many impurities still mean only one set of קרבנות. The גמרא wants to know which side of the same מחלוקת this fits.

keyTerms.meaning: And this that we learned in a משנה
Many impurities
One set of קרבנות

phrases.english: And this that we learned:
A נזיר who became impure with many impurities
brings only one offering.
Who taught it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דִּתְנַן: נָזִיר שֶׁנִּטְמָא טוּמְאוֹת הַרְבֵּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same מחלוקת to identify the author of a different משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a נזיר who became impure many times brings only one קרבן?

steps.title: רב חסדא: the משנה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the משנה is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. The case is a נזיר who became impure on the seventh day, then again on the seventh day. Since the eighth day for bringing a קרבן never came, he owes only one קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who said pure נזירות takes effect from the seventh day. You find this case when he became impure on the seventh day, and then became impure again on the seventh day. Since the proper time to bring a קרבן had not come, he owes only one קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא names רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה as the author of the משנה. He explains the exact case where the משנה's rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, pure נזירות has already started again on the seventh day. So a new טומאה that day hits a נזיר in purity, and we might think it needs a new set of קרבנות. But the קרבנות are only brought on the eighth day, and he never reached it, so all his impurities share one קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: And you can find this case
And he became impure again
The proper time (here, the eighth day for the קרבן)
Since

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא splits the two sources: the ברייתא about the seventh day follows רבי, and the משנה about many impurities with one קרבן follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Many impurities' here does not mean any impurities at all. It means impurities that keep happening on the seventh day, before the eighth day for the קרבן ever arrives.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11, using רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. The case is repeated טומאה on the seventh day, before the eighth day for the קרבן arrives, so only one קרבן is owed.

steps.title: Why the משנה cannot follow רבי
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי's view, impurity on the seventh day again and again is one long impurity. Impurity on the eighth day again and again needs a new קרבן each time. Neither case fits the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the משנה follows רבי, it does not work. If he became impure on the seventh day, and then again on the seventh day, it all counts as one long impurity. And if he became impure on the eighth day, and again on the eighth day, the time for bringing a קרבן already arrived, so he owes a new one each time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב חסדא's answer. It shows why the משנה (one קרבן for many impurities) cannot be following רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, pure נזירות only starts on the eighth day. So impurities on the seventh day never count as separate, which makes the case not truly 'many impurities.' Impurities on the eighth day happen after the קרבן time has arrived, so each one needs its own קרבן. Either way, רבי cannot explain the משנה's case.

keyTerms.meaning: One long, continuous impurity
He became impure
The time when he is fit to bring a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two days. For רבי, the seventh day is still inside the old impurity. Only on the eighth day does a new stage begin.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's ruling of one קרבן for many impurities only works under רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. For him, the seventh day already starts pure נזירות, but the eighth day for bringing the קרבן never came.

phrases.english: For if you say it is רבי,
if it is where he became impure on the seventh day,
and again became impure on the seventh day
(and again became impure on the seventh day),
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out this repeated phrase in round brackets. The point is the same either way.

phrases.english: all of them are one long impurity.
And if it is where he became impure on the eighth day,
and again became impure on the eighth day,
the time has already arrived
that is fit for bringing a קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב חסדא's answer from Step 12 by ruling out רבי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under רבי, seventh-day impurities merge into one, and eighth-day impurities each require a קרבן. So the משנה cannot follow רבי.

steps.title: What is רבי's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי's reason that pure נזירות begins only on the eighth day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי's view. This sets up the next step, where the פסוק is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, Step 10 showed how each side reads 'ביום ההוא.' Now the גמרא wants to know what in the פסוק pushes רבי to tie the new נזירות to the day of the קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from applying the dispute to asking for its source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for רבי's view that pure נזירות begins on the eighth day

steps.title: רבי learns from the order of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק first says atonement comes through the קרבנות, and only afterward says 'וקדש את ראשו.' So the new נזירות starts after the קרבנות, on the eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'And he shall atone for him for having sinned regarding the dead body,' and afterward, 'And he shall sanctify his head.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי's source: the order of the words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The atonement comes through the קרבנות, which are brought on the eighth day. Since 'וקדש את ראשו' comes right after the atonement, רבי learns that the new holy נזירות begins only after the קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall atone for him (through the קרבנות)
And afterward, then again
And he shall sanctify his head (begin his נזירות again)

phrases.english: The פסוק says:
'And he shall atone for him for having sinned regarding the dead body,'
and afterward, 'And he shall sanctify his head.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sanctifying of the head comes after the atonement in the פסוק, so נזירות starts after the קרבנות.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה pushes back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argues that if the פסוק only meant to teach this order, it could have just said 'וקדש את ראשו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: If so, let the פסוק just say 'And he shall sanctify his head.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה challenges רבי's proof from the order of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order alone would already teach that the new נזירות comes after the קרבנות. Yet the פסוק says more ('ביום ההוא,' as in Step 10). So רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה suggests the extra words must point to a different day, the day of shaving.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the פסוק say

phrases.english: And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says:
If so, let the פסוק say:
'And he shall sanctify his head.'
phrases.notes: The full פסוק goes on with 'ביום ההוא' (Step 10). He means those extra words would not be needed for רבי's point.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אִם כֵּן לֵימָא קְרָא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's proof from the order of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the order alone teaches that נזירות starts after the קרבנות, then the extra words 'ביום ההוא' are not needed. So they must teach something else.
